title: Form Array by Concatenating Subarrays of Another Array
statement:
You are given a list of integer arrays `groups` (say `n` of them) and an integer array `nums`. Decide whether `nums` contains `n` contiguous pieces such that piece `i` equals `groups[i]` element by element, the pieces do not overlap (no index of `nums` is used by two pieces), and they appear in `nums` in the same order as in `groups`: piece `i - 1` ends before piece `i` begins. Gaps between pieces are allowed.

Return `true` if such a choice exists and `false` otherwise.
notes:
## Intuition

Groups must appear in order, so the only real decision is where each one goes. Placing a group at its **earliest** match is always safe: any later spot leaves less room for the groups still to come, so it can never do better. That greedy rule removes all backtracking (which the brute force needs when it tries every placement). Each group is then just a left-to-right search in the part of `nums` that is still free.

## Approach

1. Keep `start`, the first index of `nums` not used yet.
2. For each `group`, slide a window from `start` while the group still fits, and compare it element by element.
3. On the first full match, stop; if the group never fits, return `false`.
4. Move `start` past the matched piece so the next group cannot overlap it.
5. If every group was placed, return `true`.

## Example 1, step by step

`groups = [[1,-1,-1],[3,-2,0]]`, `nums = [1,-1,0,1,-1,-1,3,-2,0]`.

- Group `[1,-1,-1]`: at `start = 0` the third value is `0`, a mismatch; at 1 and 2 the first value differs; at `start = 3` it matches, so `start` becomes 6.
- Group `[3,-2,0]`: matches at `start = 6`, so `start` becomes 9.

Both groups were placed, so the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m·L) where `m = nums.length` and `L` is the longest group: `start` only moves forward, so at most `m` windows are checked in total, each with at most `L` comparisons. KMP would make it O(m + total group length).
- Space: O(1) beyond the input.

## Pitfalls

- After a match, jump past the whole piece (`start += group.length`); moving by one lets pieces overlap.
- After a mismatch, move only one step, not past the compared values: `[2,2,3]` sits at index 1 of `[2,2,2,3]`.
- Stop the window when `start + group.length > nums.length`, or you read past the end.
- Groups must keep their order; searching each group in the whole array ignores that.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `start` | first unused index of `nums` / current window start |
| `group` | the group being placed |
| `found` | whether `group` was matched |
| `matches` | whether the window at `start` equals `group` |
| `j` | position inside the group |

narration.2: start is the first index of nums that no chosen piece uses yet.
narration.3: Place the groups one by one, in their given order.
narration.5: Try windows while the group still fits inside nums.
narration.7: Compare the window at start with the group, value by value.
narration.8: Does this value differ from the group's value at the same position?
narration.9: Yes: this window is ruled out, so stop comparing.
narration.13: The window equals the group: this is its earliest placement.
narration.17: No match here; try the window one step to the right.
narration.19: The group never fit in what was left of nums.
narration.20: So the groups cannot all be placed.
narration.22: Skip over the matched piece so the next group cannot overlap it.
narration.24: Every group found a place, in order and without overlap.
